messages.subject: Prediction with spatio-temporal model
parts:
Hi,

I'm using INLA to analyse the performances of some spatio-temporal models for irregular lattice data. I set to NA the values that I want to predict, and I use the instruction "control.predictor = list(link = 1)", but when I use this model : 

  fo <- nuovi_casi ~ 1 + f(id.provincia, model='besag', graph = g) + f(id.temp1, model='iid')
  
  m.3 <- inla(fo, data=dati, family = 'poisson', E=e, control.predictor = list(link = 1),
              control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config=T))


All the different values that I want to predict are equal. There is a matematical reason for this? With different models like:

  fo <- nuovi_casi ~ 1 + f(id.provincia, model='besag', graph = g)
  
  m.4 <- inla(fo, data=dati, family = 'poisson', E=e, control.predictor = list(link = 1),
              control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config=T))

the predictions are different one to the other.

One example of what I get is this:

giorno
vero
day                   real  prediction
2020-03-05 737        920
2020-03-06 772        919
2020-03-07 1206       1407
2020-03-08 1241       1433
2020-03-09 1535 527
2020-03-10 1132 527
2020-03-11 2541 527
2020-03-12 2479 527
2020-03-13 2212 527

Best,
Marco Franchin

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction with spatio-temporal model
parts:
From the model you cite, the prediction in time,would more or less
constant (different for each 'id.provincia').

If you want something that picks up time better, you need something else
than 'iid'.

Best
H
